card: Enforces consistent parameter naming between function declarations and definitions by enabling clang-tidy's readability-inconsistent-declaration-parameter-name check. Parameter names in headers and implementations drift apart over time, reducing code clarity. The author submitted this as an RFC, questioning whether the initial churn across 75 files is worth the consistency benefit. Based on #36743.
evidence: PR description: "Declarations and definitions tend to drift apart. We could align these, and then enforce that via clang-tidys readability-inconsistent-declaration-parameter-name check... This may not be worth the (initial) churn / we may also be fine with inconsistency here."
problem: Parameter names between function prototypes in headers and their definitions in source files drift apart over time, causing inconsistency and mild confusion when navigating code.

risk.why: Consists purely of parameter renames and giving unused-outside-TU functions internal linkage, causing no functional or ABI changes.

scope_notes: A mechanical codebase-wide refactor touching 75 files across almost every subsystem, largely consisting of single-word parameter renames in headers and NOLINT annotations on Qt signals.
summary: Enables the clang-tidy readability-inconsistent-declaration-parameter-name check and resolves mismatched parameter names between declarations and definitions across the codebase. It also removes unused serialization templates for std::unique_ptr<const T> and marks functions used only within their own translation units as static.
